newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise, fuelled by BTC jump.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise, fuelled by BTC jump.

text.p: Slovenian shares closed 0.43 percent higher on Friday, fuelled by a nearly four percent gain in warehouse operator BTC, traders said.
The SBI index rose 5.63 points to 1,315.10 but ended the week 1.5 percent lower.

"Domestic demand has been a bit higher in the past two days due to a general expectation that prices will rise in May when foreign buying is expected to resume, therefore more gains can be expected next week as well," one trader said.
But market participants warned foreign demand may not be large enough to support long-term growth.

"International investors may decide to keep away from the Slovenian market because of its unpredictability due to various sudden central bank decrees and due to the high costs of new accounts which will be between 9 and 15 percent of the amount handled," an analyst said.
Turnover rose to 49.4 million tolars from 29.3 million. Overall four shares rose and six fell, while two were flat and 15 were untraded.
Bank SKB was the most active share, closing unchanged at 50,500 tolars on volume of 317 shares for total turnover of 16 million tolras.
BTC was the top gainer, rising 3.77 percent to 13,490 tolars on volume of 73 shares on speculation the company may issue global depository receipts (GDR).
Aroma producer Etol led the day's decliners, falling 2.61 percent to 17,140 tolars on volume of 23 shares.
